experiment: #7 transfer re-validation: surrogate-generated naive-vs-adaptive PGD adversarial inputs evaluated on the production FFI-backed TFLite classifier (Raspberry Pi 5, aarch64 A76).
protocol: gen_transfer_batch.py crafts L-inf PGD (T=50, eps=0.1, alpha=0.01) against the d=42 real surrogate with the attacker-coupled (vulnerable) basis, both naive (defense view detached) and adaptive (gradients through whole defense incl. rotation+basis). classify_transfer.rs loads the real float32 TFLite classifier via the C FFI and reports flip-rate (ASR) vs the surrogate natural label. This tests adversarial-transfer to the deployed classifier, per Section VII-B limitation (gate used only the surrogate). RECALIBRATED gamma=2.3061 (corrected from deprecated 1.984 = benign P75). Prior transfer run archived as transfer_ffi_gamma1984_deprecated.json.

reconciliation.dev_box_n20_smoke: naive 0.05 / adaptive 0.30 — small-sample (n=20), NOT reliable; direction did not hold at n=200.
reconciliation.pi_n200_gamma23061: naive 0.385 > adaptive 0.270 on the real classifier — the ORDERING INVERTS vs the surrogate-side coupled-basis advantage. Direction robust to recalibration: previous gamma=1.984 run gave naive 0.380 / adaptive 0.285.
reconciliation.interpretation: Both attacks DO transfer to the real classifier (0.270-0.385 ASR vs 0.000 on originals), confirming adversarial exposure survives transfer. The naive>adaptive ordinal inversion on the real classifier (opposite of the surrogate attacker-coupled gate) is itself a finding: adaptive coupled-basis optimization is surrogate-overfit and transfers LESS cleanly; naive transfers more on average. Reported honestly as a transfer-gap contrast.
reconciliation.key_defense_fact: Transfer ASR (0.270-0.385) is well below the surrogate attacker-coupled gap the gate demonstrated, so the deployed classifier retains meaningful robustness to crafted inputs despite surrogate coupling.

sources.classifier_bin: edge/src/bin/classify_transfer.rs (built with --features tflite, CARGO_TARGET_DIR repo-root target/)
